source.title: Speak Out of Turn: Safety Vulnerability of Large Language Models in Multi-turn Dialogue
source.authors: Zhenhong Zhou; Jiuyang Xiang; Haopeng Chen; Quan Liu; Zhe-Rui Li; Sen Su

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates whether a different intervention—decomposing harmful requests across dialogue turns—elicits harmful responses from aligned models. It does not test fine-tuning or the first-token mechanism.
record.gate_note: The measured outcomes concern harmfulness in multi-turn jailbreak dialogues, not the fine-tuning, token-position, or parameter-localization claims. No results on prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes are reported. Rows record the study's own harmfulness evaluations and its single-turn comparisons.
record.test_reason: This study tests a multi-turn query-decomposition jailbreak on commercial API models (GPT-3.5/4, Claude-1/2, Gemini-Pro). It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2) and no per-token KL or aligned-versus-base comparison (V3). It does not test prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes (V4), does no parameter localization (V5), no analysis of why alignment is shallow (V6), and no deepening training (V7). Its attack works by splitting a harmful request into benign-looking sub-queries across dialogue turns, then asking the model to combine or invert its earlier answers. That is not 'getting past the opening' of a single response. The paper says it uses instruction-following across turns 'rather than affirmative initial responses.' Qi et al. (arXiv:2310.03693) appears only as a citation among works that use AdvBench. The reader's 'tests'/T2 is wrong: the study neither tests nor uses any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that current safety alignment ignores multi-turn dialogue, and that decomposing malicious queries into sub-queries across turns elicits harmful dialogues from commercial LLMs that refuse the direct request. They recommend multi-turn safety alignment and better context understanding.
record.recipe_differences: A multi-turn prompt-decomposition jailbreak; no fine-tuning or first-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with model, manual versus automatic decomposition, dialogue baseline versus role-play, evaluation judge, and number of dialogue turns. The authors report that more turns generally correspond to more harmful dialogues and higher harmfulness scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Multi-turn decomposed prompting produced harmful dialogues in all five commercial models (GPT-4 judge: 22.77%–84.12%; LLAMA Guard: 3.84%–23.55%). Adding role-play in the final turn raised these rates modestly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Splitting a harmful request across dialogue turns elicits harmful outputs from safety-aligned chat models that refuse the direct request.

fits_no_version.finding: With the same sub-queries combined into one turn, GPT-4-judged harmfulness fell (Is-Harmful 0.058–0.217). Direct AdvBench prompts were almost never answered (Is-Harmful 0–0.0057).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The multi-turn format, not only the decomposition itself, adds to harmful compliance.

record.problems: The main harmfulness assessments rely on GPT-4 and LLAMA Guard rather than crowdsourced raters; the authors note that LLAMA Guard is more conservative than GPT-4. The paper does not report uncertainty estimates in the displayed tables. It does not release its test dataset or decomposition prompts.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 2 moderation-API results, Figure 5 turn-count plots and associated text-only/figure-only outcomes, the GPT-4 harmfulness score means in Table 3 and Table 4, and the supplementary online-model case figures. Kept the principal Table 1 harmful dialogue rates and the Is-Harmful and harmfulness-score comparisons from Tables 3–4.

untested.parts: No prefilling, suffix or decoding manipulation. The multi-turn decomposition attack is a different mechanism and does not act on the opening tokens of a response.
No weight or rank analysis; closed API models only.
Speculates that multi-turn data is rare in safety SFT, but tests nothing about token-depth shallowness.
Proposes multi-turn safety alignment but does not test it.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The row states ('partial' for the role-play rows and the single-turn controls) are not judged against any claim version and carry no meaning for this phenomenon; R41–R60 are controls. No verdicts are given because no version is tested. The study could inform a separate multi-turn jailbreak phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or post-fine-tuning refusal measurement.
No benign-data fine-tuning or resulting harmful-compliance measurement.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base comparison.
No test of compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes; the study tests a different multi-turn attack.
No weight or rank localization experiment.
No test of whether data or training objectives produce token-depth shallowness.
No training intervention to deepen safety or test of whether such training holds up.
